title: OnePlus Exits US and Europe but Doubles Down on India as OxygenOS Merges Into ColorOS
excerpt: The former 'flagship killer' will cease new product launches in the West while confirming India remains central to its future, alongside a global transition from OxygenOS to Oppo's ColorOS.
body:
• OnePlus will stop launching new products in the US, Canada, and Europe, making the OnePlus 15 the last device sold in those markets
  • India operations continue as planned, with the recently launched OnePlus N6 and upcoming N6x confirmed on the roadmap
  • All existing OnePlus devices globally will transition from OxygenOS to Oppo's ColorOS with the Android 17 update
  • The restructuring follows Oppo's broader consolidation of OnePlus and Realme into its core brand

End of an Era in the West

OnePlus has confirmed what rumours had signalled for weeks: the brand is ending new product launches in the United States, Canada, and Europe. The announcement, posted on the OnePlus US and India Community Forums, marks the conclusion of the company's decade-long effort to compete in Western smartphone markets with its "Never Settle" philosophy and aggressive pricing.

The OnePlus 15 becomes the last device to launch in these regions. Existing customers will continue receiving software updates, security patches, warranty coverage, and after-sales support for their committed support periods, backed by parent company Oppo. Customer service channels will remain operational. The North American Community website and app will shut down on August 16, 2026.

India: The One Market That Stays

In a separate announcement, OnePlus confirmed that India — one of its largest and most loyal markets — will continue business as usual. The company highlighted recent product launches and confirmed upcoming devices, including the OnePlus N6x, as part of its active Indian roadmap.

OnePlus has carved a significant niche in India's smartphone market, particularly in the premium and upper mid-range segments where it competes with Samsung, Apple, and fellow BBK Electronics brands like Realme and Vivo. Its after-sales support in India has already been quietly merged into Oppo's extensive service network.

However, a Bloomberg report has suggested that Indian operations may also cease by 2027 as Oppo completes its consolidation, with China remaining the only standalone market. OnePlus has not addressed this claim directly.

OxygenOS to ColorOS: The Software Merger

Beyond the geographic restructuring, OnePlus confirmed a significant software change: all eligible devices globally will transition from OxygenOS to Oppo's ColorOS with the release of Android 17 later this year. Users will be able to voluntarily upgrade, with the option to roll back to OxygenOS if preferred.

The move formalises what had been increasingly apparent since 2021, when OnePlus merged OxygenOS with ColorOS at the codebase level while maintaining separate branding. Over the years, the two skins became nearly indistinguishable in functionality, making the brand distinction largely cosmetic. OnePlus claims the unified approach will accelerate software update rollouts and improve overall software quality.

What It Means for Indian OnePlus Users

For the millions of OnePlus users in India, the immediate impact is limited. Devices will continue to receive updates and new products will keep launching. The shift to ColorOS branding, while symbolically significant for brand loyalists who valued OxygenOS's cleaner approach, is unlikely to change the day-to-day experience given the already-converged codebases.

The bigger question is whether OnePlus as a brand survives Oppo's consolidation beyond the next year or two. For Indian consumers who built loyalty around the brand's value proposition — near-flagship specs at competitive prices — the devices and support will continue regardless of what name is on the box. But for the brand community that defined OnePlus's early years, this restructuring feels like a final chapter.
nri_angle: OnePlus's exit from the US directly affects NRI users who rely on the brand across regions; India remaining as the priority market reinforces the country's growing weight in global consumer tech strategy.
author: Diaspora Desk
